thread:
olivia (support): heads up — customer ACME hit a big rerank outage during their peak this morning. p95 jumped from ~180ms to 2.4s under sustained qps ~1.2k and a bunch of requests ended up 504 gateway timeout. filing here with sample request ids and payloads.

raj (customer-eng): thanks. which rerank model / config are they using? bulk vs per-request? do we have any rate-limit headers in responses?

olivia (support): model: mm-rerank-v2-1 (8k). they're sending candidate sets ~500, client-side batching at 64. no client backoff configured (retries=3 immediate). sample curl we captured:

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "x-request-id: acme-20260314-1" \
  -d '{"query":"best widgets","candidates":[...500 items...]}'
```

maya (eng-runtime): I pulled logs for acme-20260314-1 window. We see many upstream 502/504 from gateway -> rerank-backend. Worker queues show long tail (`queue_latency_ms`) and several kernel-level stalls around the same time. KV-cache hit rate dropped ~70% -> 12% (prefetch miss storm).

sre-bot: deploybot: canary rollout mm-rerank-v2-1 completed at 2026-03-14T08:02:12Z (no autoscaling events flagged).

zach (eng-sre): can you paste a sample backend log snippet for a 504? also need pod-level metrics (cpu, iowait, gpu utilization) for the window.

olivia (support): snippet: 

```
[2026-03-14T08:12:34Z] request_id=acme-20260314-1 stage=gateway -> upstream_time_ms=3014 upstream_status=504
[2026-03-14T08:12:34Z] backend=rerank-worker-17 log=error "kvcache miss, candidates=500, batch=64, seq_len=0"
```

maya (eng-runtime): that upstream_time lines up with worker GC/alloc spikes and KV cache eviction churn. Hypothesis: huge candidate lists + large batch sizes cause KV cache thrash and force more expensive compute path, which increases tail latency under high concurrency. Also noticed client retries amplified the QPS (retry storm).

raj (customer-eng): customer admits they recently raised candidate size from 200 -> 500 to improve quality. can we give short mitigation steps we can tell them?

maya (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: reduce candidate set to <=200, lower client batch_size to 8-16, add exponential backoff with jitter on retries, and enable prefix/KV caching for common prefixes. Platform mitigations: apply temporary per-customer rate limit and enable circuit-breaker on the gateway route for heavy hits.

zach (eng-sre): longer term: add autoscale triggers based on queue_latency_ms and kvcache_miss_rate, add a per-route soft limit we can bump in Dedicated plans, and expose a client-side recommended limits doc for large candidate counts. I'll open an incident and create a runbook entry.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1879 "ACME rerank 504 tail latency" assigned to eng-sre, eng-runtime; pager escalated.

olivia (support): i will relay mitigations to ACME and ask them to run a staged rollback to candidate=200 + client backoff. can we also provide a repro harness so they can test?

maya (eng-runtime): yes — use the staging rerank cluster (staging-rerank.redwood) with this artillery snippet to repro load:

```
config:
  target: "https://staging-rerank.redwood/v1/rerank"
  phases:
    - duration: 300
      arrivalRate: 200
scenarios:
  - flow:
    - post:
        url: "/"
        json:
          query: "test"
          candidates: ["...repeat 500 items..."]
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer sk-STAGING"
```

maya (eng-runtime): when reproducing, capture `queue_latency_ms`, `kvcache_hit_pct`, `worker_util_pct`, and `gateway_retry_count`. If repro successful, we'll try reduced batch sizes and candidate windows to confirm latency improvements.

raj (customer-eng): thanks — i'll coordinate with ACME to test the smaller candidate window and apply client backoff.

zach (eng-sre): action items: 1) run repro on staging (eng-runtime) 2) add per-route soft limit and temporary throttle for ACME (infra) 3) update runbook + client-recommendations doc (product/docs) — I'll own incident.

olivia (support): perfect — updating the customer and will post progress here. :thumbsup:
